chunks: With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Everything has a door, and the door of the grave is at the side of the feet. When you place the جنازة, then place it from the side of the feet. The deceased is taken out from the side of the feet, and du'a is made for him until he is placed in his niche and the soil is leveled over him.

key_terms.التُّرَابُ: the soil placed and leveled over the grave
key_terms.الرِّجْلَيْنِ: the feet side, indicating the direction from which the deceased is inserted
key_terms.الْجَنَازَةَ: the funeral bier or deceased brought for burial
key_terms.الْقَبْرِ: the grave in which the deceased is buried
key_terms.بَابٌ: an entrance or access point; here, the designated entry of the grave
key_terms.حُفْرَتِهِ: his burial cavity or grave hollow

ai.seo_question: How should the deceased be placed into the grave according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the prescribed manner of bringing the deceased to the grave and placing him into it. It indicates the etiquette of entering the grave from the side of the feet and continuing du'a for the deceased until burial is completed.
